Call recap (short):
- Workload: product search + summarization for 25M monthly queries (peak median seq len ~120 tokens).
- Current ask: target effective cost goal ~ $800-$1,200 per 1M tokens after optimizations.
- Key lever: prefix caching for search prompts + KV caching for session-based summaries.

Our assumptions we used in the call (attached spreadsheet has the full breakdown):
1) Baseline token mix: 40% prompt tokens (short), 60% completion tokens (longer).
2) Prefix cache hit rate: conservative 35% first pass, with optimization to 50% by tuning prefixes and TTLs.
3) KV cache hit rate for sessions: ~20-30% initially; higher for repeat users.
4) Effective unit math: unit $/1M tokens uses weighted mix and cache-hit adjusted token counts (we apply a 50% cost for cached tokens since cached responses still incur minimal compute for retrieval metadata).

Immediate next steps I promised:

Hi Alexa \u000e2\b0\t4 answers inline + attached updated sheet with a short note on the cache-cost accounting.

Q1) Rationale for treating cached tokens as ~50% cost:
- Retrieval cost: a cached prefix lookup still hits memory/disk (depending on TTL/eviction) and some CPU to reconstruct the prompt; we model that retrieval as ~10-20% of full generation cost.
- Reduced transformer compute: cached prefixes avoid the autoregressive decoding for those tokens (this is the dominant cost). Conservatively we assume cached tokens reduce GPU time by ~60-70%.
- End-to-end: if retrieval + partial CPU + small overheads sum to ~30-40% of full generation, modeling cached tokens at 50% gives a conservative buffer for infra overheads and cross-region retrievals.

Q2) Effort to hit 50% prefix hit rate:
- Short answer: moderate (2-3 sprints of eng time across your search + infra teams).
- Steps: 1) canonicalize queries (normalize whitespace, stopwords, product aliases) \u000e2\b0\t4 mostly client/server side parsing. 2) implement prefix-key hashing and a short-term TTL (5-30min) in the request path. 3) add a small warmup job to seed top queries.
- Dependencies: need read access to query logs and a small infra change to route cache lookups before calling the model endpoint.

I attached version v3 which includes two scenarios: 
A) Conservative scenario: prefix hit 35%, KV/session hit 20% => effective $/1M tokens = $1,150 (illustrative).
B) Optimized scenario: prefix hit 50%, KV/session hit 30% => effective $/1M tokens = $880 (illustrative).

Notes in the sheet show the math: we calculate raw token count, subtract cached token-equivalents (applying the 0.5 factor), and then compute model compute cost + small retrieval/infra surcharge. The sheet includes sensitivity toggles so you can see the effect of hit rate +/-10%.

Next steps:
- Marcus will scope the integration work (ETA for scoping: Tue 03/02).
- Aditya to schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (please propose availability next week).
- If procurement wants a committed quote, I can produce a 12-month reserved proposal using the optimized scenario; we typically add a conservative buffer in the SLA pricing.

Let me know if you'd like us to run a short sample (1 week) on a subset of queries to empirically measure prefix hit rate before committing. That would reduce risk and tighten the numbers.

Best,
Marissa
